messages:
jenna-customer: Hey team — since ~03:10 UTC our customers on the eu2 dedicated pool are seeing 95-99p latency spikes and occasional 429 errors from the inference API. Only on Dedicated, hosted endpoints are fine. Example: 2026-03-15T03:12Z request id abc123 returned 429 throttle_exceeded. Any quick checks?
sara-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the pool id + a short repro request? Also confirm if this is a single customer or multiple tenants in the same reserved pool.
jenna-customer: Pool: eu2-dedicated-small. It's one customer running multiple pods. Repro: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","input":"hello"}' -> intermittent 429 or 1.5s -> 8s tail latency.
mike-eng-sre: @jenna-customer thanks. Can you run these on the node that served abc123: `kubectl get pod <pod-name> -o wide` and from the node run `nvidia-smi mig -l` and `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` ? Want to see MIG instances and per-process GPU usage.
jenna-customer: Running now, output snippets: 
```
$ kubectl get pod inference-abc -o wide
NAME           READY STATUS   RESTARTS NODE          NOMINATED
inference-abc  1/1   Running 0        eu2-node-17

$ nvidia-smi mig -l
GPU 0: 2g.10gb (3 instances active)
GPU 1: 1g.5gb (1 instance active)

$ nvidia-smi pmon -c 1
# gpu pid type sm   mem   enc   dec  command
# 0   1234 C  98%  10240  0     0   /usr/bin/python3 server.py
# 0   2345 C  70%   5120  0     0   /usr/bin/python3 worker.py
# 1   3456 C  5%     400  0     0   /usr/bin/python3 light.py
```
jenna-customer: dcgm metrics show sustained high sm_util on GPU0 across the period.
mike-eng-sre: That looks like a classic noisy-neighbor: multiple pods ending up on the same physical GPU / MIG instances saturated. Do you have pod anti-affinity or topologySpread configured? If not the cluster autoscaler may pack onto fewer nodes when capacity is tight.
david-ml: Also check our dedicated autoscaler logs — if scale-in/scale-out aggressiveness is set low it can lead to packing. Ask to collect `cluster-autoscaler` events and `redwood-dedicated-controller` logs for the timeframe.
sara-support: Quick mitigation options: 1) Add soft anti-affinity or topologySpread to spread pods across nodes. 2) Increase pool capacity (temporary) so pods get scheduled to other nodes. 3) If using MIG, prefer allocating pods to different MIG slices: we can set a scheduling constraint that prefers distinct physical GPUs.
mike-eng-sre: Can you run `kubectl describe node eu2-node-17` and `kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod,involvedObject.name=inference-abc` and paste relevant lines? Also capture `docker stats`/container metrics if possible.
jenna-customer: Pasted event lines: `Back-off scheduling due to Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` a few minutes before spikes. Node describe shows 3 MIG instances consumed on GPU0 and 1 on GPU1.
mike-eng-sre: That confirms it. Autoscaler allowed pods to pile onto eu2-node-17 while GPU1 had less capacity available. Suggest two changes: 1) add `podAntiAffinity` with topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname for these deployments; 2) tweak autoscaler to prefer scale-out when `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` appears frequently.
sara-support: I'm going to open an internal ticket to review autoscaler config and add a short-term pool scale-up. Creating support ticket SUP-4582 and pinging runtime team. :eyes: @mike-eng-sre can you own the eng follow-up?
mike-eng-sre: I'll take it. I'll also add a small admission webhook suggestion to prefer spreading MIG allocations (low-risk change). Can you temporarily increase the pool min replicas by +2? That should reduce contention while we patch scheduling.
redwood-oncall-bot: Incident SUP-4582 created by sara-support — priority P2. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4582
jenna-customer: Increased min replicas +2 did reduce 95p from ~1.2s to ~420ms in the last 10m. No more 429s. We'll keep monitoring and send the requested logs.
sara-support: Great — next steps: (1) eng runtime to propose scheduling change, (2) ops to review autoscaler thresholds, (3) customer to monitor for 24h. We'll update SUP-4582 with all logs and a repro. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
